notes.title: 🚨 Update 1.2 is Live! 🧟‍♂️ “No Plan Z” DLC is Out! 💥 Plus a 30% Discount!
notes.content:
Hey everyone,

Update 1.2 for No Plan B is now live! I’ve added new Skirmish missions, fixed some long-standing bugs, and launched a new DLC: No Plan Z!

Oh, and to celebrate, No Plan B is 30% off for a limited time.


✨ What’s New in 1.2

New Skirmish Missions
This update brings in a new batch of Skirmish missions, one for each scenario of each faction, making it 19 in total. More challenge and more chances to test your planning under pressure.


[carousel autoadvance="true"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/11b64a9a1b5a85658ff75b4dd1fbc993ab2b7ef4.png"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/056c36edf452ae391b7fc31864a329efbc8484c1.png"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/31eac7b69f47b0426c12598db0fb44a107911f1b.png"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/f1aa6e73a1a84a93aa51ebfd577ffe57e9bae095.png"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/95497f9b7c330f4c5b08cf1f9a023322e9870e52.png"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/c19451e5d3b70a2bbe6210bb5ba8d5403823253d.png"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/80b6a7158a2127437c75ada45469855cb9a69529.png"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/121088d37d07a5aa230a5eeff4facd8e16afedff.png"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/ca29ab96e0d62533fb4c616dfc5c968f55a12165.png"][/carousel]

Important Fixes & Improvements
Thanks to your feedback, I’ve squashed a few nasty bugs that may have disrupted your experience during the planning phase:

Snipers' field of view now correctly account for vision through windows.

Grenades throws no longer get cancelled when using the undo feature while planning.

Fixed the first FBI mission having a VIP to save instead of an objective to take 🤦‍♂️


🧟‍♂️ No Plan Z Is Out Now
No Plan Z is a new DLC for No Plan B and it takes the tactical gameplay you know into zombie territory. The rules are the same, but the stakes are higher, and survival is never guaranteed.

Here’s what to expect:

A new kind of threat: Your enemies have been infected by a deadly virus, making them weaker but faster, more aggressive, and far more numerous.

Unpredictable behavior: Infected enemies won’t hesitate to charge your squad head-on or spit infected blood from a distance, forcing you to adapt your tactics.

New Skins: Each faction gets new unique skins to tweak your style and dive deeper into this new universe.


[previewyoutube="rUeEZxHUGso;full"][/previewyoutube]


If you've ever wondered how your tactics hold up when the enemy doesn't think or stop, this is your chance to find out.

[dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/2660340/No_Plan_Z/"][/dynamiclink]Note: Once you purchase the DLC, Zombie Mode will be enabled by default for all your existing squads. You can disable it at any time in the squad settings.


💥 30% Off for a Limited Time
To mark the launch of No Plan B 1.2 and No Plan Z, No Plan B is 30% off!

If you’ve been on the fence or want to bring friends into the squad, now’s the time.


🙏 Thanks for the Support
As always, thank you for playing, reviewing, and sharing feedback. It means a lot, and it helps me continue building and improving the game.

I hope you enjoy the new content and I can’t wait to hear what you think.



Stay tactical,
– GFX47

notes.title: No Plan B Patch Contest
notes.content:
Calling all operators!

No Plan B is adding some new cosmetic patches to the game, but we need YOUR help.

Starting right now until JULY 25th, submit your custom drawn design to the dedicated Discord channel to have a chance at getting your design added into the game!
The number of winning designs depends entirely on the number of people who participate, so the more participation there is, the more likely your design can be worn on operators worldwide!

Rules


 All drawings must be original and cannot be stolen or be of an existing design to avoid copyright.
 Design must be square or round in shape, and have a minimum dimension of 512x512 pixels.
 Artwork must be digital and in the PNG or JPEG format.
 The contest will take place in two stages. The first stage is the submission stage where we gather everyone's designs. Once the date to upload designs has ended, we will have the voting phase, which will be about three days long.
 We will create a Google form to gather all the submissions and allow everyone to cast their votes on their favorite designs.
 We will announce the winners at the end of the voting period!



Remember that patches in the game are small, so keep designs relatively simple.

Good luck and happy designing!

notes.title: No Plan B 1.1 "Path of Serenity" Update
notes.content:
Retryable Campaign Missions

I heard your frustration regarding the campaign's requirement to restart the whole chapter upon failing a critical mission.

Failed campaign missions are now retryable by default BUT the map and enemies will be regenerated.
Damage taken by your squad during failed missions will not be saved anymore to give you a fair second chance under the same conditions.

Note that if you prefer how it worked in 1.0, you can disable it using the "No Try B" squad option.

New Unlock Path

I also realize that even if it's the core of the game, the campaign can be a bit too challenging for new players. Besides, skirmish missions are a smooth transition between the tutorial and the rest of the game.

In this regard, I've changed the way game modes are unlocked so that new players can test their tactics on a few easy standalone missions before tackling the real deal. The other game modes will be gradually unlocked following the skirmishes.

Here's the new unlock path in details:

 Skirmish missions are split into 4 groups, completing each group will unlock the next one
 Completing the tutorial unlocks the first group of skirmish missions for all the factions
 The 1st group unlocks the campaign
 The 2nd group unlocks the custom missions, including modded ones
 The 3rd group unlocks the challenges
 The 4th group unlocks the mission generator
 Each chapter of the campaign unlocks the next one, the 5th one unlocks the survival mode

You shouldn't lose access to any of the modes you've already unlocked in 1.0 though.
Please let me know if it's not the case.

UI/UX Improvements

Based on your precious input, I've incorporated the following improvements:

 The number of each character now appears above them, corresponding to their keyboard shortcut
 The selected character displays an animated selection marker to help you identify who you are using
 The color of the selected character's field of vision now accurately indicates the weapon's accuracy over the distance
 It's easy to miss a recently unlocked attachment slot when it is on the left side of the weapon, so I added a flashing arrow pointing to it
 Squad options can now be changed mid-run
 You can now exit the squad selection screen with the cancel button or the escape shortcut

Balancing

Some balancing changes based on your feedback:

 I reduced the maximum range of the weapons to make them more specialized and reduce the effectiveness of close-range weapons in large rooms (this does not change the optimal range or maximum accuracy)
 The range of the stun effect on enemies when kicking a door has been increased when you don't have the "Door Smasher" skill as it was too rare to see it happen
 Enemy threat level in skirmish missions now increases gradually
 Reduced the size of the map for recruitment mission in chapter 2

The Details

Finally, I've removed the default iron sights from the Peace4 and Raven weapons when equipping other aiming attachments and moved back the aiming attachment slot of the GG36 weapon.

Full changelog

This update also comes with a lot of improvements and fixes detailed in the following posts:

https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1269020/view/6292166527289251270
https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1269020/view/6292166527292486215
https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1269020/view/4181104663290552813

Let me know what you think of this update in the comments.

notes.title: No Plan B 1.0 is officially out! 🎉
notes.content:
[previewyoutube=-vFDQPVzk24;full][/previewyoutube]

I'm thrilled to announce the official launch of No Plan B on Steam, following a highly successful early access phase with an impressive 90% positive reviews!

In No Plan B, the challenge is to carefully plan your team's tactics in close quarters battles.
Use the timeline to synchronize each door breach, grenade throw and room entry with precision.
Watch your team execute your plan autonomously in epic cinematic replays.
Take on challenging roguelike campaigns or standalone missions.

It launches with a 10% discount available for one week:

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1269020/No_Plan_B/

Thank YOU!

I'd like to express my infinite gratitude to the 20,000 Early Access participants who contributed to shaping the game into its 1.0 state.
A special acknowledgment goes to the testers who dedicated a significant amount of their time to reporting bugs, help me enhance the game design, and refining its balancing over the course of 2 years.
Additionally, heartfelt appreciation is owed to the translators whose efforts made it feasible to release the game with support for 22 languages.

Supporter Edition

The game launch is synchronized with the release of the "Supporter Pack" DLC, bringing a range of new character customization options to boost the tacticoolness of your squad and make your mission replays even more epic.

Please note that purchasing this DLC primarily demonstrates your support for the game and the customization options don't provide any gameplay advantages.

https://store.steampowered.com/bundle/23899/No_Plan_B__Supporter_Edition/

The DLC joins the "Supporter Edition" bundle alongside the full game and its soundtrack.
Good news: players who purchased the bundle before the release should automatically receive the DLC.

V1.0 Changes

Here are the changes introduced by 1.0:

 New Character Voices: the 4 factions now have both male and female voices, recorded by the awesome Ivy Moody (SWAT/FBI female voices), Hannah Melbourn (Robbers/Gangsters female voices), Brian Watts (SWAT/FBI male voices) and Jarret Griffis (Robbers/Gangsters male voices).
 New Keyart: It was a great honor collaborating with Gray Shuko on the creation of the new key art. I sincerely hope you enjoy it!
 Game Modes Unlock option: begin the game with all game modes unlocked.
 Seasoned Squad option: max out your characters' XP.
 Persistent XP option: retain their earned XP when restarting a campaign chapter.
 Hollywood Mode option: breach rooms fearlessly, facing enemies who seem to have forgotten how to aim.
 Performance Optimizations: while I'm not claiming the game will run smoothly on a potato, you should notice significant improvements in performance, particularly on larger maps.


Other Bundles

I'm also hosting the "GFX47 Games" bundle that contains both Gladiabots (my previous game) and No Plan B.

notes.title: No Plan B "Smooth Sailing" Update (Beta 16)
notes.content:
Campaign Unlock Choices

During the campaign, weapon, grenade and shield unlocks now give player the choice between several randomized options instead of predetermined items. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/53dbefed99be647e3188335ed8d2d1701fae1396.jpg
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/27214629d521f24588773e268e39b87f6b446da0.jpg
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/591dd513c76345aee78598572b5556eb670badee.jpg

Victory Ranks

A new rank system has been implemented to give the player a better sense of achievement when completing a mission. This applies to all game modes.

The S Rank can be reached by completing all mission objectives and taking no damage to either your agents or civilians.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/ca4fe5b0f33cf386b925766c4c8f8715a0616579.jpg

This will double the XP reward in campaign missions.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/e082c1b45a1e3c8aabb7d2c5c42fc14469d30b4f.jpg

XP Balancing

Speaking of XP, the thresholds for character skills and weapon type specializations have been lowered. This means that skill points and specialist levels for weapon types will be easier to unlock.

The speed at which weapon attachments are unlocked has been reduced. But they are now correctly mentioned in campaign mission reports.

Improved Paths

The size of the pathfinding grid has been reduced to allow smoother path drawing.
A new simplification pass has also been implemented to straighten the trajectories.
In the same spirit, the auto-path (double click or shift+click) has been improved to allow shorter, more direct paths.

Here is a before/after comparison of the way paths are drawn:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/ad556bd136ff17c3f138795aecf0f35b8167d091.gif
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/e440285a7071f1047c5b1aef5b7f0a1b98547b2e.gif

And a comparison of the final paths:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/3d8a968c2237a316ccc105a37a4fb2ec3b820d09.jpg
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/1e4841e863ba848fdd50268ecf6bfbc2f372d294.jpg

Biomes

An early version of the biome system comes with Beta 16.
A biome defines the mood of a map generated by the game. Each biome uses a set of room types. Each type determines which props will be used in these rooms.

For instance, the "Bank" biome uses the "Vault" (max 1 vault per map), "Office", "Lounge" and "Corridor" room types. Money stacks, gold bars and security gates will only appear in the vault while flower pots or water fountains may appear in corridors or offices.

Here is an example of a Vault room generated inside the Bank biome (used in the “stop the heist” scenarios):

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/1e7c0de803a48a8beed91c5e0b4184e0fe09f3ea.jpg

notes.title: No Plan B "Roguelike" Update (Beta 15)
notes.content:
DISCLAIMER
This update will reset your progress!
But don't panic, the save files are now placed in a different location, so you can go back to the "beta14" branch and get back where you were (in Steam, right click on the game, properties, betas).
Please note that this branch will remain on the Beta 14 build, won't be updated and will ultimately be removed to switch everyone on the latest build.

New Campaign

But Why?

I've been incrementally updating the campaign since it's been in the game.
The thing is, it never really allowed me to fully achieve what I had in mind in the first place.

The idea is to build the best possible squad throughout the campaign, within its generated constraints.
As Early Access progressed, the game became more focused on collecting as many credits as possible to unlock the entire arsenal and max out your characters.
Plus, once you've completed the campaign with one faction, there's no real incentive to try again and experiment with different approaches.

That's why I completely reworked it in this update.

But How?

The credits system has been completely removed.
Weapons, grenades and shields are now obtained by completing specific campaign missions.
They became a little more faction specific again, but I kept a few that spanned multiple factions.
The same goes for recruiting, as you now start with a team of 2 members, keeping the maximum team size at 8.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/c1ca1a6ff9c404f147b0e4ec5d7eed1cfd22dae2.png
Using a weapon with any member of your team will gradually unlock more attachments that are now free to equip. It will also improve their handling of the weapon type.
Skill upgrading now uses skill points earned by deploying the character in campaign missions.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/da35f6aaba039b8e7e4e2848f17e7a3f29ca9007.jpg
The fatigue mechanic was also removed, as it was too strong a constraint that forced the player to choose their team composition to mitigate it instead of adapting to the mission at hand.
Persistent damage still exists, so you'll still need to manage your injured characters. But they now automatically recover 20% of their health between missions. The Medic skill can now increase this percentage for the whole team!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/cb69b8f001888affbb30579407ec48f9a2a85950.jpg
All progress is now reset when restarting a campaign chapter.
This includes the equipment gained, the XP earned and the recruited members.
It will also fully heal the incapacitated characters or recruit new ones to replace them if you play in permadeath mode.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/9f91bbb484fad39c1639f241afb8308c715da95d.png
Once you've completed the campaign, your squad has reached its final form.
Deploy them in the many other game modes and see if they can compete with the other teams on the leaderboard!
Or create a whole new squad and try a different approach to the campaign?

New Gameplay Options

You will now be able to compete on leaderboards regardless of which difficulty or option(s) you use.
However, the rankings are broken down by configuration. This means that you will only face squads that play under the same conditions.

Guns, Lots of Guns

This option gives you access to the Armory where you can freely pick any weapon, grenade or shield of the game, from all factions. It also unlocks all the weapon attachments from the start.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/9ec3f7f67802498aac6102cc70953ec71274da36.jpg
Obviously, this makes the equipment unlocks during the campaign unless.
If you don't want to go that far and try out a specific loadout before unlocking it in a regular playthrough, you can also access it in any practice mission.

Full Squad

Start with a full set of 8 characters.
However, you will not be able to recruit new ones during the campaign.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/b007400b42d4e22720e6ec7442c752678b2113f1.jpg

notes.title: No Plan B "Special Operations" Update (Beta 13)
notes.content:
Crouching

You can now crouch, greatly reducing your move and rotation speeds, but making your movement silent, improving your accuracy and making you much harder to hit.

But the real benefits are numerous.
You can line up 2 characters in the same direction and double your firepower.
Protect your crouching teammate while they interact with doors or use grenades.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/d40d24083ba160927f86294b0fc3eb8fcaf16a0a.jpg

You can also hide while crouching to sneak around enemies, reducing your engagement range and surprising them.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/e0b7542b711a17805f189c7bdd6ff0f93a102019.jpg

Last but not least, you will increase your coverage when behind objects.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/7f5de8beea863c859e4dfd663dfcf58b7f3b9460.jpg

Perks Accessibility

The feedback on the perks was pretty clear on Discord: perks are too expensive to be used in the early game.
Activating perks will no longer cost credits but will instead reduce your mission score.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/324984e360ccc6113969cc1b61a6668e4abdf2cf.jpg

Each Map Scan (still limited to 3) will remove 10% of your final score, Deafening Strike 15%, Tear Gas 20% and Night Raid 25%.
These penalties are cumulative.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/3593553e845b1b47ccde45968fa1efa5704dfd35.jpg

New Scoring System

The scoring formulas have been changed once again to accommodate different map sizes.
Instead of having a fixed number of points for each objective completed, the score will take into account the ratio of objectives completed.
For instance, instead of having 1000 points for each objective, you will receive 3000 points x ration of completed objectives (objective completed / total objectives).

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/2b716f8ec23b8d7c6464cce2cf518ef339bd4db0.jpg

Overall scores should be higher (as well as the credit reward on your first try!).
Therefore, all rankings have been reset.

Squad Management

Now, a highly anticipated quality of life improvement: managing your squad from the main menu without having to launch a mission.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/eb81bd4ce9841f1a4f97c4b956207e720c44e568.jpg

Another cool feature is that the game now saves the last equipment used by your characters and automatically loads it the next time they are deployed in a mission.

Saving Replays

Tacticool replays take time to craft.
The good news is you can now save them locally and improve them later, share them with your friends and other players on Discord or simply cherish them :D

notes.title: No Plan B "Progression" Update (Beta 12)
notes.content:
DISCLAIMER
This update will reset your progress!
But don't panic, the save files are now placed in a different location, so you can go back to the "beta11" branch and get back where you were (in Steam, right click on the game, properties, betas).
Please note that this branch will remain on the Beta 11 build, won't be updated and will ultimately be removed to switch everyone on the latest build.

New Progression System

Game Modes and Equipment

Game modes, weapons, grenades and shields are now unlocked by completing campaign missions.
Once you've unlock something, it will remain unlocked for all your squads, independently of their faction.

The campaign now has 5 chapters for each faction (instead of 3) with increasing threat levels. The different map features (windows, transparent doors, exterior maps and storeys) are progressively introduced during the first chapters.

Please note that you can't unlock features from 2 campaign missions of the same level in a single chapter. This will become possible once you complete the whole campaign.

Weapon related Skills and Attachments

Weapon specialist skills are now unlocked by using the type of weapon in campaign missions.

Weapon attachments are unlocked by using the weapon in campaign missions. Their unlock order is randomized.

Squad Members

The initial team size has been changed from 8 to 4 members. Additional members can now be recruited during the campaign.

Each character now has a predefined set of 3 skills they can be leveled up using credits.
Players can manually choose each recruit amongst 3 candidates (or reroll, using credits) when creating a new profile or unlocking a new recruit in the campaign.

Scoring

The score of the first try on each mission now determines the credit rewards and the leaderboard rank.
The score computation formulas of the different mission objectives have been unified and the cost of pretty much everything has been increased to match this new reward system.

Other Important Updates

 Permadeath and Sandbox are now options of your squad (profile) instead of a separated difficulties
 Sandbox unlocks all weapons, attachments, grenades and shields
 Reworked the main menu UI
 Changed the initial arsenal for each faction
 Grenades are not consumed anymore in campaign missions
 Characters cannot shoot while running anymore

notes.title: No Plan B "Smart Ass" Update (Beta 11)
notes.content:
Smarter enemies

I reworked the whole AI system for enemies, fixing many existing bugs and improving their behavior significantly.

New events

They now react to nearly 20 different types of events.
Some of these new events include the sound of shots from their teammates, the sight of their teammates getting killed, the sound of a sniper shot, or the noise your agents make when moving near them (the faster you move, the easier they hear you).

New reactions

Their reactions are also more elaborate.
They won't just rush to the position of the event but, depending on their archetype, will instead seek for the best compromise between defending their initial position, approaching the threat and preparing for you to step through that door, finger on the trigger.

Archetypes distribution

Additionally, the archetypes used by your enemies are now specific to the mission objective instead of the game difficulty. They will be defensive in hostile clearing missions and a more agressive in infil/exfil ones.

Hard/Permadeath difficulties

Hard and Permadeath difficulties push the slider even further with enemies running away from exploding grenades, hiding from snipers, and even waiting for you behind cover!

Arsenal changes

To help you deal with this new breed of NPCs, I tweaked the initial arsenal of each faction to add more grenades and a sniper rifle.
Your characters can now carry 1 additional grenade, making it 2 by default and can carry up to 4 thanks to the Grenadier skill.

Good luck!

Weapon Customization

You guessed it, this update is all about giving your arsenal more personality.

Attachments

You can now customize your weapons with various attachments, including:


 Stocks

 Red dots and scopes

Complete more missions to earn more credits and spend them wisely!

Stealth

Imagine how deadly you could be with the Night Raid mission perk!

Choose your style:


 Plain colors
 Shinny metals
 Camo patterns

notes.title: No Plan B "'SPLOSIONS" Update (Beta 8)
notes.content:
This one's gonna blow!

New Grenades

We'll never have enough grenades, right?
So here are new ways to mess up with your foes...

Shock Grenades

Derived from the Stun Grenade, the Shock Grenade will shock (really? shocking!) agents in the area of effect.
When shocked, agents have reduced speed and accuracy.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/d79c1e90b038f176302691106dbdd232077ec4c2.jpg

Thunderbolt Grenades

The Thunderbold Grenade is a more accurate and deadly variant of the Frag Grenade.
Useful when you want to be 100% sure that a certain area of the map is empty.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/6b794204479294542e1346c9ad9ceecc3b202513.jpg

Storm Grenades

The Storm Grenade, on the contrary, has a large area of effect but deals less damage.
Your new tool of choice for weakening hostiles in large rooms.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/80ba9dc9762912b4d7e142cd837c7883d8cc4644.jpg

Decoy Grenades

The Decoy Grenade will make a lot of noise, pulling enemies towards it.
Placed correctly, it will give you the upper hand when you walk into the room and everyone turns their backs on you.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/3ab27ced6c2945dbb5f3d24c466095dd81cddc55.jpg

Stinger Grenades

The Stinger Grenade will have the opposite effect and knock them away from the area by casting painful rubber balls.
Ideal for clearing a path or moving any threat from a specific area.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/00b612ba453d764f82dd0d869af4a13f30273bab.jpg

Skills

Skills can now be unlocked using credits (previously called "weapon points") instead of skill points.
From now on, the campaign missions will instantly reward you with credits.
This should give you an earlier opportunity to forge your squad's specialties.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/aba6f406d623c3733b0c5336cd8acf5123df273b.jpg

New Skills

The level 3 of the Designated Marksman skill has been added, providing a wider field of view and allowing you to monitor more windows.

Shield lovers will also benefit from the new Tank skill which improves their speed.

Merged Skills

The following skills have been merged into a single one:

 The Grenadier and Quarterback skills
 The Door Smasher and Lock Picker skills
 The Runner and Agile skills


Perks

Perks can also be purchased using credits!
The other big difference is that most of them can now be used in any mission (Skirmish, Random, Challenge, Custom and obviously Campaign).

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/fb134e31d4633144d3bad6db401da10738359e66.jpg

Also, new perks are finally here!
They'll give you a big advantage, sometimes with a few drawbacks, giving you the opportunity to play the game a bit differently.
Be careful though, each perk will only apply for one try and are pretty expensive (prices subject to change depending on your feedback). So make it count!

Squad Heal, Squad Rest and Arsenal Resupply will remain campaign specific, as they don't make much sense outside of that context.

Deafening Strike Perk

Deafens enemies, preventing them from reacting to sounds during the mission.
This perk will allow you to sneak around without attracting surrounding hostiles. It should prove useful in escort missions ;)

Night Raid Perk

Attack in the dark of night after cutting off the electricity to the building.
Enemies will have very limited vision range, unlike you and your tacticool night vision goggles 8)
They will, however, slightly limit your field of view. Be extra careful when checking your corners!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/9e6eaa77c5885f7d524c714f14dd192c434134a5.jpg

Tear Gas Perk

Spray tear gas into the ventilation to disorient the hostiles inside the building.
Their field of view and accuracy will be significantly reduced.
Your gas masks will protect you from these effects, but breathing through them will impact your speed.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/57514f37544b50d28e2a61f9f0f0bed091595e8f.jpg

Map Scan Perk

This one is not new but has been reworked a bit.
You can now use it a maximum of 3 times on each mission. Each time you use it, it will improve the accuracy of the approximate position of hostiles and civilians.
Note that civilian positions will no longer be predicted by default and if you want to use lethal grenades you will probably have to scan beforehand to avoid collateral damage...

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/3fa5d8eb0d8cd4b240e7e08e69415d569cfe7f83.jpg {STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/57178706db6229f34c5f80f49be681468116237d.jpg {STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/a789f5cf8afa3857a9542a864619a57e1b8e30f0.jpg

UX Improvements

2 long-requested features are finally coming to the game...

Locking the timeline

You can now lock the timeline using a toggle, replacing the (good old) Control key you had to hold down until now.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/62e2eb5ab03e89a5ad7c1fb281abf81751572b1d.jpg

Note that you can still use this toggle with the Control key shortcut.

Isolating the selected character

Isolate the selected character with this new toggle, replacing the Alt key.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/6bbc6e429b78a1899d42fe605ecd2ab65515badc.jpg

Note that you can also use the Alt key shortcut to toggle it.

Full changelog

notes.content:
What's up folks!
I hope you liked the Halloween Game Event. Zombies may make a come back in the future, stay tuned ;)

New Objectives

I've worked on 2 new objectives: escorting targets out of or inside the building.
You'll have to protect one or several individuals and guide them to the designated areas, like you did with your operators in infiltration or exfiltration missions.

As a result, each faction gained new playable scenarios, 6 in total:

SWAT / HVT Exfiltration

Escort the High Value Terrorist out of the building. Considering their profile, it's not such a big deal if they take a few damage on the way. Just make sure they make it to the exit so we can "extract" intels from them.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/fe5aa333592fc75b4d6ed85363f26781be0aea19.png

SWAT / Bomb Defusal

The Bomb Squad has arrived, your objective is to clear the path to the explosives for them. Their bulky suits can absorb a limited amount of damages but make them quite slow to move. Make sure they can start working on the objectives in time!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/f5a8e55331579a06fb76dd6f48591c1c3a480bb0.png

Robbers / Taking The Loot Home

We deactivated the alarms, took care of the guards and reached the safe. The only thing to do now is to bring this big pile of cash to our hideout. Protect your mules and get to the exit as soon as possible!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/526d9e66b3ed5ee2da0627a8f52ff8ac0e64ef91.png

FBI / Hostage Evacuation

Before we can stop the ongoing heist, we need to get the hostages to safety. Protect them at all cost along the path you choose to the exit!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/79c455a94fa225812235565fecfcbb4b8951c307.png

FBI / VIP Exfiltration

This Very Influential Politician found out a little late that they shouldn't have done business with a gang to help them climb the ranks... Escort them out of this trap before their associates end their negotiation.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/89a3a5a142956882aaaab19bd3af0e382206e093.png

Gangsters / Get The Boss Out

The meeting between your boss and their rival didn't quite end as planned. Guess there was only room for one toilet paper lord... Now you need to get out of their HQ before their minions make you pay for it.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/15739685141b241c3b020e8019d6d9aa314289e6.png

Melee Enemies

notes.title: No Plan B "Play It Your Way" Update (Beta 6)
notes.content:
The New Profile/Squad System
Ever wanted to try another approach on the campaign or reset your squad skills but didn't want to lose your progress? It's now possible with the new profile/squad system!
You can have as many squads as you want, each with its own faction and difficulty level (more on that in the next chapter).

Your progress from Beta 5 should be automatically imported into squads with the default "normal" difficulty.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/4255221c64177c6077e138d41b8658ffe1a9d8f1.jpg

Important note: weapon and skill points are specific to each squad.

New Difficulty Levels

When creating a new squad, you get to choose its name, the faction and the difficulty level you want to play.
The game now has 5 difficulty levels:

 Chill: Enemies are more defensive, do not master their weapons well, and are slow to react
 Normal: Enemies are quite defensive and you have the edge on weapon handling and reaction times (this is the difficulty level you're used to play)
 Sandbox: Same setting as the "Normal" difficulty with infinite weapon and skill points
 Hardcore: Enemies are more aggressive, shoot as well as you, and react almost as fast
 Permadeath: Same setting as the "Hardcore" difficulty with permadeath during the campaign

Note: leaderboards are now split between difficulties.

Other Important Changes

Weapon Points
The initial weapon points for each squad has been increased from 1500 to 5000 points, allowing you to buy additional weapons, grenades or shields from the beginning.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/ec646cd2ee14e4c245c5af47e3e853dfc05e0286.jpg

Aiming Improvement
The aiming system has been reworked to prevent agents from stopping in place to adjust their orientation. They now anticipate direction changes in advance so they'll be facing the right direction when you planned it.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/6f5712bec7e9e5cd879a7edc84ba14c1f021e311.gif

Grenades In Stairs
It is now possible to toss grenades from one floor to the other! The angles are still pretty tight but it will allow you a safer approach of these deadly stairs.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/15c49285dbafb4a5e2f4822ee26ceae6d325d8f9.jpg


Unequip Skills
You can unequip skills from your agents in the setup screen and replace them with new ones. However, the skill points you've spent won't be refunded.
The goal is to make you think twice about the specialization of your agents while allowing some late-game tweaks.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/acb02331e3ef4a7e3e4c8a3b3c6923da519e7d90.jpg

Civilians
Planning to use a frag in the next room? What if there are civilians in there?
The approximate position of civilians is now shown on the map to help you prepare for this eventuality. A bit like the "scan" perk reveals the approximate position of your enemies.
Their position won't change when replanning a mission so as not to mess up your existing plan.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/f18a9d8b447bc46956d72b5ddc13c191fcc2390a.jpg

Better Team Size Limit Enforcement
You can now select the agents you want to deploy from your full squad, even in missions with a team size limit. The number of occupied/available places is displayed in the top left corner of the screen.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/ca0b9da428731cffe4cdccbebe7dbdab0693a287.jpg

Contextual Help
The loading screen has been improved to have a progress bar and a scenario related background instead of the help videos that could be laggy because of the loading process.

These help videos will now be displayed in context and will only use a part of the game screen.
For instance, the first time you launch a skirmish mission, you will get the video explaining how to deploy your agents. When 2 of your agents will be very close to each other, you will be explained how to display only the plan of the selected agent.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/875eb080687aafe4b1c5bb2ab856051906a767e2.jpg

Game Menu
The game screen now has a menu you can access by hitting the escape key or using the top right corner button. It frees some space for the game UI.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/b72b18467226bd21036f45cd9eabae894121bd8f.jpg

Leaderboards Reset
The security of the leaderboards has been improved to prevent cheaters from pushing fake scores and stealing the top ranks.
Unfortunately, the leaderboards had to be reset in the process.

Undesired Door Kicking
The bug that caused your agents to kick doors without being ordered to do so has been fixed!
Many thanks to the testers who helped find the cause of this very frustrating bug.

notes.title: No Plan B "Verticality" Update (Beta 5)
notes.content:
Multi-Storey Buildings

Time to add some verticality in your tactical gaming, folks!
NPB now plays in 3D for good with the addition of 2-3 storey buildings.
Obviously, along with them will come the deadly stair cases! The map generator uses several types of them, offering more or less concealment and view angles.
You'll love to hate them XD

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/495ac8ac25892357419e2e0583038f17e294d489.jpg
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/b4a8ef588059b887ccb978d3609d0ec6d7786a05.jpg
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/1efdd8dc63b31d931dd7c5c957211d899d0ad027.jpg
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/045a4238fcf0b8cc2ed29681bf5d66b1167805d4.jpg

As you can see, I also added some roof top entries to a few of the buildings to offer new ways to approach your missions.

The map editor was improved for the occasion to make it easier to work on several floors.

New Replay Cameras

You can now use 5 different replay cameras to make your successful missions even more tacticool:

 The "Free" camera is the one you're already used to: you can move freely around the map with any focus on a specific position.
 The "Position" camera, which is anchored to the position of the selected agent. It will keep the camera angle you've defined. It's place over the head by default but you can adjust it.
 The "3rd person" camera, which is anchored to the position AND the orientation of the selected agent. It's placed behind the right shoulder by default but you can adjust it.
 The "1rd person" camera, which is also anchored to the position and the orientation of the selected agent. It's pre-placed and oriented to mimic the view in a FPS game but as usual, you can adjust it.
 The "Weapon" camera is pretty straight forward as it will stick to your weapon. Position and angle can also be changed.


Here's a demo using each of them:
[previewyoutube=8-mcCRQtCNE;full][/previewyoutube]

Note that you still blend and cut between the different views you will configure.

Balancing

Weapons

Most of the weapons have undergone significant changes to their stats in order to make battles more dynamic.
Assault rifles in particular, have now faster aiming but slow down your agent's rotation.

Enemies

The reaction time of the enemies has been reduced and their number increased.
The goal here is to make it easier to surprise them, while maintaining the importance of bringing enough agents to the party and checking every corner.

Weapon point rewards

I heard your feedback, weapons are too expensive.
That's why I added weapon point rewards to the random and community missions.
I also increased the rewards of the skirmish and challenge ones.

Free tip: don't forget to buy more grenades to help you during the campaign ;)

Full changelog

notes.title: No Plan B Content Update (Beta 3) + Discount
notes.content:
Are you ready for this second major update on the early access?
I think you're not.

Difficulty Tweaks

This game, its campaign in particular, is a beast, I know. It's actually how I wanted it to be in the first place! But, thanks to your feedback, I realize it can be frustrating for a lot of you, that's why I decided to tweak the difficulty down a bit.

Here is a list of the most important changes:

 Characters incapacitated during the campaign missions don't die anymore and are still available when starting a new chapter
 Skills points are now wons by each participating character (still available after completing a chapter)
 Characters now start the campaign with 3 skill points
 Reduced the overall difficulty (+10% aiming duration for enemies)
 Tweaked the faction modifiers (less maluses on the bad guys)
 Civilians are now be present in the "High Threat" difficulty missions (SWAT and FBI factions will fail the mission if any civilian is killed. The other ones will get away with just a score malus)


Ballistic Shields

This was one of the most requested features, it's now a reality!

The 4 new ballistic shields will protect you and your teammates from frontal incoming fire.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/350f7247957bce73d83168ad1ae858d726594dc3.jpg

Each shield has it's own authorized weapon types, some can only be used with handguns, others support SMGs...

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/e6a493824695cf0426d4433bee1a3df3257bb564.jpg

...and the heavy one (more suited for team protection) will require your agent to forget about attacking!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/0f495dc6327c832e490070278c03c8f988b1837d.jpg

Every faction doesn't have access to those shinny babies so they have to make up their own. Cheap but still effective!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/d503ea2aeb00514280cae1ae1f2bc565a70dd218.jpg

The counterpart for most of the shields is obviously slower movements and rotation, making it difficult to defend against lateral or rear threats. Be sure someone covers your 6!

Sniping Spots

The snipers received some well deserved love in this update: they can now be deployed on specific spots where they won't be reachable by enemies and have a good angle on the external windows of the building.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/29036d3284d05232c150a86ecad23ca7ceea9599.jpg

Agents on sniping spots are their to support the rest of the team and can't move from their position.
Obviously, only sniper rifles are authorized on these spawns.

New Shops

In order to differentiate the 4 factions of the game even more, each of them now has its own shop with a specific set of weapons, grenades and shields.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/d484b23c447e367a4ee8b69ecd6bcfef147afced.jpg  {STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/43e9fdbc1ce205b430382badcc029d407dabe7dd.jpg  {STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/49aa24fd3cc97858a4acc16cbe605c08a1f41b53.jpg  {STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/318d84ae128a8ecad21f42c74c24dabfcde72c95.jpg

The shop UI also received an important usability update: the ability to easily compare weapons. Right-click on a specific weapon to select it then place your pointer over another one to compare their stats.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/b89b46c4ed9ffc157ecac13a062cfb50cbcc91cc.jpg

As you can see, the weapon tooltips now show their detailed stats.

New weapons

In those new shops, you'll find 5 brand new weapons:

The "Light50", aka "tank killer". Fortunately, there's no tank in the game...

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/42026645131b7645a953c9dc7e03996646774a94.jpg

Another long distance killing machine for the bad guys, the "W40".

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/7a28aebce288a39bcd61e598b3bd8aff4b9262da.jpg

The "Twins" won't give you much choice, run or die.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/15f22e3bff856ca4df60d1ba72ea2d57698ac3e6.jpg

The "Blaaka47" is the most precise AR so far, be sure to keep your distance though...

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/8e76a0313f91ff7df08402fdd64bcee16a4d1b3b.jpg

Fan of the old mob movies? You should like the "Chicagun" ;)

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/fd1cef836319ab2d24baeda6f1c5db46d5bdbaa3.jpg

I've also tweaked the stats of all the weapons to better highlight their differences.

Special Discount

To celebrate this new major update, the game will get a 10% DISCOUNT FOR 2 DAYS.
Get it while it's hot and tell your tactical savvy friends about it!

Note that this discount cumulates with the soundtrack bundle, so you can get the bundle for almost the regular price of the game alone.

notes.title: Map Editor Update (Beta 2) + Special Discount
notes.content:
The first big update of the Early Access is finally here!

Special Discount

To celebrate that, the game will get a 10% DISCOUNT FOR 2 DAYS.
Get it while it's hot and tell your tactical savvy friends about it!

Note that this discount cumulates with the soundtrack bundle, so you can get the bundle for almost the regular price of the game alone.

If you've followed the recent updates on the test branch, you are probably already aware of what is in this update but I'll detail it anyway for those who didn't.

The Map Editor Update

So, as the name suggests, this update is focused on the in-game map editor that you can use to make your own missions and share them with the rest of the community.

More than 5000 new map elements have been added to the map editor: new walls, buildings, furniture, vehicles, props, etc.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/628d5cc5cdec8b8c8c837231e5b854cf7ff01406.png

All of them have not been integrated in the skirmish missions and the map generation system yet, so you won't see them in the challenge, randomized and campaign missions either. I'll introduce them in the map generator incrementally as I'm improving it.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/185358b76f92650b823bd155b315f046a44a5cbc.png

A big part of the game system had to be reworked to support all those new possibilities and the crazy ways I've seen them used in the community maps (like using walls as debris or props as walls for instance). It took me more time than I expected but it also allowed me to improve things that weren't initially planned. The most notable is the possibility to make maps with different heights for the walkable surfaces, passing under them, etc.

Quality of Life Improvements

I also wanted to highlight some changes unrelated to the map editor.

Reordering the game sections

The first one is about the difficulty of the campaign. In your feedback and reviews, I often read that the game throws you a bit harshly from the tutorial to the campaign with a 8 characters team to handle and a bunch of new rules you didn't expect.

I've actually designed the skirmish missions with increasing team size, map size and difficulty to prepare the players for the campaign. The thing is most players launch the campaign as soon as they have completed the tutorial, probably because the way the main menu as been designed incites them to do so.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/fef1e7dae87d047cc4526e709defd08237077d9a.jpg

So I've changed the order of the different game sections and the home buttons to put the single missions before the campaign, hopefully it will change the default behavior of the new players.
I could lock the campaign until you complete some (or all) the skirmishes but I suppose it would be frustrating for those who feel up to the challenge... Let me know what you think in the comments.

Changing the timeline behavior when switching characters

The second important change is about the way the timeline acts when you select a character. Until now, it would reset to the time of the character's last action. I've noticed in the different videos and streams of the game that it's often not the expected behavior and leads to planning mistakes.
That's why I've changed it so that selecting a character doesn't change the position of the timeline anymore.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/7fdfe496e6c260abb0c3f03b6fd097219fdab63d.jpg

I've also added an option in the settings to switch back to the previous behavior in case you find it more convenient that way.

Full changelog

Below is an exhaustive list of the changes coming with this update.
I know there's a lot to take in, so I've done my best to highlight the most important ones:

New features and content

 Added 5000+ new map elements!!!
 Implemented support for elevated grounds navigation
 Added the option to reset (or not) the timeline when selecting a character (disabled by default)
 Added primitive map elements (cube, sphere, cylinder, etc)
 Added the blood toggle option in Settings/Graphics
 Added the screen shake toggle option in Settings/Graphics 
 Added an error message when clicking on the execute button and the mission objective is not complete by the end of the plan
 Added help sections for handguns, sniper rifles and weapon points Wait for the tutorial videos to finish before displaying the play button


Improvements

 You can now rewatch completed campaign missions (only applies to missions completed after this update)
 Removed the map size limits in the map editor
 Removed the weapon point reward when completing a campaign chapter BUT added weapon point rewards to the challenge missions
 Disabled skill unequipping, clicking on an equipped skill now opens the skill shop panel allowing you to upgrade your equipped skills or unlock and equip new ones
 Disabled throwing grenades through windows
 Scroll the timeline using the mouse wheel (slowed by holding Alt, accelerated by holding Shift by default, see settings)
 Automatically saves cinematic configuration (camera shots)
 Display the next mission button in the game over screen of campaign missions, leading back to the chapter screen
 Improved the exit mission and replan mission button icons
 Increased the button backgrounds transparency
 Prevented weapons and grenades to overlap each other on the weapon rack
 It's now possible to rotate weapons and grenades on the weapon rack without having to drag them first
 Temporarily removed the ATMs from the possible map generator props
 Improved the light and material inspectors in the map editor
 Walls are now split in 2 faces, you can have different visuals on each side
 Doors are now separate assets, you can put different doors 
 Improved the main menu buttons
 Added a new type of large interior window in the map generator
 Changed the order of the main menu headers
 Made the scale of the NPC Spawn Zone model independent of the zone size
 Improved the camera obstacle hiding system (increase the width of the hiding effect as you tilt the camera down)
 Improved the default placement of newly bought weapons and grenades
 Lowered the default mission settings object position
 The execution phase now starts paused, allowing player to configure the camera before launching the replay
 Wait for the video to end before displaying the play button in the campaign helps
 Improved the SFX when clicking a button that launches a mission
 Updated the translations

The Roadmap

Happy new year, NPB squad! 🎉
I see my previous post was pretty popular and you posted quite a lot of suggestions, that's great!

After merging similar requests and replying to some comments, I've set up the roadmap for the early access. It lists the features that I'm currently working on, the ones that are planned for later, and the ones still needing your opinion or subject to reflection on my side.
You can check it out here:
http://roadmap.noplanbgame.com

Please note that the order in which features are displayed doesn't necessarily indicate the order in which they will be implemented. It will mostly depend on the technical dependencies between them and their development complexity.

Also, the roadmap is dynamic, so don't stop posting your ideas (just make sure it has not been already posted) and voting for others right here:
http://suggestions.noplanbgame.com

The First Update

As you can see on the roadmap, the first update will focus on the map editor. It was not the most upvoted suggestion but something I already started working on before releasing the early access, it was just not ready yet.
Basically, I'll add more (much more) assets to the existing library and improve support for bigger, more "exotic" maps.

notes.title: Early Access launch date announced!
notes.content:
No Plan B will launch on Steam Early Access on DECEMBER 1ST, 2021!

For the occasion, I've recorded a commented gameplay video explaining the core concepts of the game and giving you a glimpse at what to expect from the early access version:

[previewyoutube=rCjX9cBI_Ts;full]https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rCjX9cBI_Ts[/previewyoutube]

There's even a french version if you speak baguette de fromage.

I'm sure you have a lot of questions about this whole early access thing. Well, don't fret, I have some answers for you...

Why Early Access?
The main goal of Early Access is to involve the Steam community in the development process and get their feedback and suggestions for the game.

Approximately how long will this game be in Early Access?
It is expected to last around 12 months depending on player feedback and the amount of content that will be added.

What is the current state of the Early Access version?
The Early Access version already has all of the base game mechanics implemented and balanced in a polished state and free from major bugs.

It includes:
- Tutorial missions
- 4 factions (SWAT, FBI, Robbers and Gangsters)
- 4 types of mission
- 5 types of weapon (23 weapons in total)
- 3 types of grenade
- Mission editor + community made missions

For each of the 4 factions:
- 3 campaign chapters (30 missions in total)
- 9 skirmish missions
- daily, weekly and monthly challenge missions
- 4 random mission generators (1 for each type of mission)

How is the full version planned to differ from the Early Access version?
The plan is to tweak the existing game mechanics if necessary and add more content:
- New game modes
- New game mechanics
- New types of mission
- New map biomes
- New campaign perks
- New character skills
- New weapons, grenades and equipment
- Weapon attachments

Will the game be priced differently during and after Early Access?
The price will not change when the game leaves Early Access.

How are you planning on involving the Community in your development process?
I will be giving regular updates on the development process and actively listening to player feedback before and after each update.
The official Discord server will be the main communication channel but I'll also monitor the Steam forums.

I have another question!
Let's post it in the comments below!

What to do in the meantime?
You can try the free demo available on the Steam page, talk about it with your friends, share it on your favorite internet places and most importantly, you know the drill:

notes.title: More details about the gameplay
notes.content:
Many of you asked me how this "No Plan B" concept is actually working, so I guess it's time to give everyone more details about it.
Please note that I'm still prototyping the game, so nothing of what follows is set in stone!

You'll have 2 ways to play the game :

Single mission mode
As you already thanks to the game description, missions will be designed by the community. I'll be part of the community, so I'll design some of them myself of course.
In the single mission mode, you'll pick one of those missions. You'll be able to order and filter them by popularity, difficulty, upload date, creator, etc.

Once the mission starts, you'll have to build your team from your character deck (more on in another post), choose their equipment and plan your every move and action in a single plan. Think of it as the "single plan" challenges in Door Kickers:

[previewyoutube=xnU0Q9my1qs;full][/previewyoutube]

If your plan fails, you'll be able to retry the same mission BUT with a different RNG seed, meaning the map will be the same but the NPCs will spawn in different locations, have different behaviors, different weapons, etc. The goal here is to keep the same layout but offer a different challenge and prevent players to "die and retry" the missions until they succeed.

Campaign mode
The game will work a bit differently and become a bit more hardcore in campaign mode.

First of all, campaigns are sets of missions (selected from the missions you can play in single mission mode) organized kinda like the sector maps in FTL:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37092585/bd494e5144ae2b04f87687beb36dd0dd45345634.png

Each spot on the map is a mission with a specific objective type, level of difficulty and a set of potential rewards in case of victory.

The main difference in this mode is that you'll have only one chance per mission, only one plan, NO PLAN B!!! \o/ (sorry)
Complete the mission and you'll earn perks that will help you in the rest of the campaign. Fail and one of your team members may be injured or even perma-killed!
Did I tell you, you will have to complete the whole campaign with the same team? The good news is you'll be able to deal with it by using healing or character replacement perks between missions (more on that later too).

So, the challenge in campaign mode is not only to complete a series of missions but also to prepare your team and choose your path wisely, balancing risk versus reward and optimizing your chances of success on the long run.

Alright, I think that's enough information for a first post, I'll detail the other gameplay mechanics in other ones ;)
Stay tuned by adding the game to your wishlist 👇
